html:
The Kiliwa are a Yuman people of northern Baja California in Mexico, in the dry mountains and valleys southeast of Ensenada, around the Sierra San Pedro Mártir.

They lived by hunting deer and bighorn sheep and gathering agave, pine nuts, acorns and seeds, moving between the mountains and the desert with the seasons. Dominican missions founded in the late 1700s, such as San Pedro Mártir and Santa Catalina, drew some of them in, and disease cut their numbers sharply. The Kiliwa language is close to extinction, with only a few elderly speakers. Their neighbours include the Paipai and the Kumeyaay to the north and west, and the Cochimí to the south.
sum: The Kiliwa are a Yuman people of northern Baja California in Mexico, in the dry mountains and valleys southeast of Ensenada, around the Sierra San Pedro Mártir.
